key_insight: UniMotion is the first single model that jointly understands and generates human motion, natural language, and RGB images by representing motion as a continuous signal (not discrete tokens), preserving temporal continuity and avoiding quantization errors.
problem_solved: Existing unified models only cover restricted modality subsets (e.g., Motion–Text or Pose–Image) and depend on discrete tokenization that introduces quantization artifacts and breaks temporal coherence; UniMotion enables fully joint, high-fidelity multimodal understanding and generation across Motion, Text, and Vision.
method: Single unified architecture with shared latent space and cross‑modal encoders/decoders to handle motion, language, and images within one model.
Continuous motion representation (rather than discrete tokenization) to preserve temporal continuity and reduce quantization error for generation and understanding.

Joint training objectives for both understanding (e.g., retrieval, captioning, classification) and generation (e.g., motion synthesis from text/image, image-conditioned motion), plus cross‑modal alignment mechanisms.
impact: UniMotion simplifies multimodal pipelines and improves quality of motion generation, retrieval, and cross‑modal reasoning by eliminating tokenization artifacts and enabling richer joint supervision—beneficial for animation, HCI, robotics, and multimodal research.

paper_title: UniMotion: A Unified Framework for Motion-Text-Vision Understanding and Generation
paper_authors: Ziyi Wang, Xinshun Wang, Shuang Chen, Yang Cong, Mengyuan Liu
